steps.text: Place sugar, lime juice, butter, and lime zest in the top of a double boiler; stir over medium-high heat until butter melts.
Temper eggs by mixing 2 tablespoons hot lime mixture into eggs, stir to blend.

Reduce heat to medium until water simmers. Slowly whisk egg mixture into the lime mixture. Cook over the double boiler until lime mixture thickens and coats the back of a wooden spoon, 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool slightly and spoon into a clean, glass jar. Cover and refrigerate.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Lime Curd
raw_recipe.description: This lime curd recipe is a twist on traditional lemon curd, using limes instead to make a sweet and tangy treat for cakes, scones, cookies, and more.
raw_recipe.name: Fresh Lime Curd

review.reviewBody: This curd was absolutely delicious! To make it as a filling for Key Lime Cake, I substituted 1.5 Tbsp of lime juice for lemon juice and to make sure it would hold up as a thick filling, I sprinkled in one tsp. of flour while heating. Wonderful Recipe!
This was a super easy receipe. The taste was great. The only thing I did was pour thru a strainer after cooking. It gives it a more finished look!

This is a great curd recipe (it makes an excellent sour curd with the perfect sweetness) and there's really no need to modify it but keep in mind, the key limes you use could affect the taste. I usually only use about 3-4 small limes (and only ripe ones). I grate about 2 tbs of rind then juice the limes but I mainly use "Nellie and Joe's Famous Key West Lime" juice from concentrate (in the pale green bottle) to provide the bulk of the lime juice. People seem to think fresh lime juice is automatically better but i disagree (you can always count on Nellie and Joe's juice to taste perfect). I love the extra kick that the zest gives so i add more than 1 tbs. Other than that, I follow the directions exactly (i use a glass bowl on a boiling pot of water for my double broiler), cook it the full 20 minutes, cool it about 5 and stick it in the fridge, and you'll have no problems with it being too runny or thin.

Excellent Curd! I used persian limes as that is what I had. I used all the zest of 2 large limes, so I had more than a tablespoon of zest-but I really like zest. Putting a little of the lime mixture into the eggs until they were warm but not cooked worked well. It only took about 8 minutes to cook through and set. I also made 2 cups total curd. I sterilized 2 cup size mason jars and had two jars full. I used this in a lime cheesecake recipe that I made using Knox gelatin. I made the cheesecake, allowed it to thicken then folded in some of the cold curd. Poured on to a ginger-oat Scottish shortbread crust (recipe from King Arthur Flour). None of these recipes did I follow exactly, but the curd made the dish! Thank you.

This was great. I usually make lemon curd, but had a bowl full of key limes in the house. I had great success with putting my immersion blender into the eggs in a bowl prior to adding them to the lime juice mixture. No need to put through a sieve with this technique. I added one drop of green food color and this was perfection!

Do not be discouraged by those who said it did not set for them, I made it for the first time and it came out amazing, just be patient and cook it at low to medium heat until it thickens up very good, once its cold it will set, it is on the tart side so if you want it sweeter perhaps add more sugar and taste before combining it with the eggs and yes the mason jar is upside down to show it did set.

Wow ! My first curd of any kind attempt and it was perfect, even though necessity called for omitting zest (was using « old », faded, hard limes) and mixing granulated sugar, caster sugar (1/4 c each) and allulose (1/2 c). Tangy, citrusy and sweet but not really identifiable as lime flavor. Green boost for a visual cue probably would’ve helped and lime zest definitely would solve that. Thickened with no problem after 12 min on double boiler (photo) but I continued stirring to 15 min mark, then turned off heat and continued stirring over double boiler til the 20 min mark. Let sit on residual heat till 25 min timer rang. Set beautifully by evening (ie 7 hours)

Looking at this w/fear I plunged ahead: Put a metal bowl over boiling water so it was just touching. Mixed everything: turned down to mid simmer. Thought 20-25 min was too long but it is good. Did not stir constantly but did keep close watch. I strained/jarred. It is lovely & quite delicious. I MUST comment that THIS IS NOT FOR THE FAINT OF HEART. This has a substantial kick & aftertaste you get only from citrus. If you are not a key lime fan, choose something else. I see now why the curds are as popular as they are in UK, but this is a deliciously wicked taste for now

I LOVE this recipe. This was my first time making any sort of curd, and now I wonder why I waited so long! This is simple and delicious. A couple of tips: to help prevent the egg from "scrambling" when added to the hot mixture, place the whole eggs in a mug of warm water at the very beginning of starting this recipe. That way the eggs will blend together much more easily. Whisk constantly while SLOWLY adding the eggs. 
 I used the curd in mini tart shells. I left half plain and half I poured melted chocolate into before adding the curd. Next time I will add a few fresh blueberries!

SUPER YUMMY and perfect flavor! I used Nellie & Joe's key lime juice instead of fresh. I was lazy & didn't use a double boiler. I ended up with a few little bits of egg in my finished curd. VERY easily remedied by straining the curd & it turned out perfectly. I will add more than 2 T of the mixture to temper the eggs next time. I used it to top a key lime cheesecake & it was a huge hit!

I stirred everything together and cooked stove-top for twenty minutes then strained. I reduced butter to 2 tablespoons because I don't like a greasy curd. I used 5 domestic limes to get the 3/4 cup of liquid. Finished product, after straining = 8 oz.
I loved it apart from the missing step 3. I could not believe that the most crucial part of the recipe is blank. 🫣
First timer lemon curd a success...so yummy! I followed exactly the same ingredients and method, turned out perfect and I received so many compliments. Thank you for sharing your recipe🥰
this is very very good. Make sure to use at least one tart lime. The flavor and texture of this curd is wonderful. I used it in a Pavlova. It was perfectly balanced in flavor.
Yes 🙌 Easy, never fails
I added extra grated rind for additional tang! Yum.
This curd is so good! Very easy recipe. Didn’t change a thing. It’s delicious
It was easy, it worked, it thickened up faster than expected. Most intense taste that can't be found in any grocery store product.

Great flavor. Ran out of lime juice on the cheese cake I was making so I used lime-aid and squeezed one lime and used all the zest from that lime .Still came out great. Added food coloring to green it up.

I had extra limes and hate wasting food. I googled what to do with excess limes and this popped up. I had everything on hand to make it and it was easy, fast and delicious. Tart, sweet, tangy and smooth and creamy. I’ll use this on plain nonfat Greek yogurt to make it like key lime pie. Thanks for this great recipe!
